summary: Iteration 5 retest of iter4 HIGH bug fix (/lock signOut redirect). BACKEND: 89/89 pytest tests pass end-to-end when run with -n 1 --dist loadfile (JUnit at /app/test_reports/pytest/pytest_iter5_all.xml). NOTE: pytest.ini currently pins -n 2 --dist loadscope which distributes CLASSES within a module across workers, breaking module-level state sharing (STATE dict, module-scope 'token' fixture) in test_delegates.py, test_multi_identity_wallet.py and test_fiskid_api.py — same tests then look like 41/89 failing (pre-existing infra bug, NOT a code regression: same tests pass under loadfile or single-worker). FRONTEND: The defensive fix E1 applied (useEffect(() => { if (!token) router.replace('/welcome'); }, [token, router]) on /lock, /set-pin, /settings) introduces a HIGH REGRESSION: the guard fires during AuthProvider's initial loading phase (loading=true, token=null before storage rehydration completes) on ANY page-reload or direct navigation to those routes. Reproducible on all three screens: (1) After completing register→skip onboarding→edit-back→dashboard, `page.goto('/settings')` → redirected to /welcome despite valid token in storage. (2) After setting PIN and getting to /dashboard, `page.reload()` on any of these routes → /welcome. (3) `page.goto('/set-pin')` with a fresh valid token in AsyncStorage → /welcome. Because reload after PIN setup now lands on /welcome instead of /lock, the original TEST 1 (tap lock-signout on /lock after reload → /welcome) could not be exercised via the reload path — but the sub-flow settings→Blocca ora→/lock→lock-signout could not be fully confirmed either in the same run because reaching /settings via goto is blocked by the same race. Root cause: the useEffect predicate must also gate on !loading (or on a hydrated-token flag) — otherwise loading=true, token=null is indistinguishable from signed-out. Recommended fix: change to `useEffect(() => { if (!loading && !token) router.replace('/welcome'); }, [loading, token, router])` in lock.tsx, set-pin.tsx AND settings.tsx (and expose `loading` from useAuth() — already exists in AuthCtx).

minor.issue: addopts=-n 2 --dist loadscope splits classes of the same module across workers, breaking module-scoped 'token' fixture and module-level STATE in test_delegates.py, test_multi_identity_wallet.py, test_fiskid_api.py. Under this config 41/89 fail with KeyError:'auth'/'share_token' or missing dev_reset_token. Under `-n 1 --dist loadfile` all 89 pass. Recommend switching addopts to `--dist loadfile` (still parallel across MODULES) or making fixtures session-scoped and self-contained.

ui_bugs.issue: REGRESSION from iter5 fix: `useEffect(() => { if (!token) router.replace('/welcome'); }, [token, router])` fires during AuthProvider initial loading (loading=true, token still null in state before AsyncStorage rehydration finishes) — so any reload or direct navigation to /lock, /set-pin or /settings kicks a valid signed-in user out to /welcome. Reference: /app/frontend/app/lock.tsx:22-24, /app/frontend/app/set-pin.tsx:28-30, /app/frontend/app/settings.tsx:21-23. Fix: gate on !loading && !token and include loading in the deps: `const { token, loading, ... } = useAuth(); useEffect(() => { if (!loading && !token) router.replace('/welcome'); }, [loading, token, router]);` The `loading` boolean is already exposed by AuthCtx (src/auth.tsx:8,27,51,107).

Original iter4 HIGH bug (tap lock-signout on /lock → stuck on /lock) could NOT be re-verified end-to-end because the new regression above prevents reaching /lock via reload after PIN setup (it now bounces to /welcome first). The redirect itself is theoretically wired via the same useEffect — but that useEffect is now firing at the wrong time, so we cannot confirm the intended flow works from the user's perspective. Once the loading-race regression is fixed, this test should be re-run.

action_items: (HIGH) Fix loading-race regression in /lock, /set-pin, /settings. Replace the three useEffect guards with a version that includes `loading` from useAuth() and only redirects when `!loading && !token`. Deps array must include `loading`. Without this the app is unusable on any page reload of a locked/secured route.

(HIGH) After the above fix lands, re-verify: (a) reload after PIN set → /lock stays on /lock; (b) tap lock-signout → /welcome with headline 'Mai più…' and welcome-register-button visible; (c) goto('/set-pin') with valid token stays on /set-pin; (d) goto('/settings') with valid token stays on /settings; (e) after signOut, all three routes correctly redirect to /welcome.

(MED) Consider changing pytest.ini addopts from `-n 2 --dist loadscope` to `-n 2 --dist loadfile` so module-level fixtures/state are honored, or refactor tests to be class-independent. Currently the config causes false failures in CI parallel runs.
critical_code_review_comments: lock.tsx:22-24 — useEffect(() => { if (!token) router.replace('/welcome'); }, [token, router]) needs to observe `loading` too. In the current form it fires with `token=null` during the AuthProvider bootstrap window (auth.tsx:37-53) and races past the storage-rehydration set().

set-pin.tsx:28-30 — same defect as lock.tsx; additionally the redirect can fire while the register/login navigate is still in-flight because expo-router's SPA navigation reuses the same AuthProvider only within the same tab session (any goto/reload restarts the loading cycle).
settings.tsx:21-23 — same defect; also note useFocusEffect(load) will re-fire on remount and could interact oddly with a partially-loaded auth state.
auth.tsx already exports `loading` via AuthCtx (line 8, provided at line 107). No new plumbing is needed — just consume it in the three screens.

server.py forgot-password path guards dev_reset_token under ENV=='development' (line 455). This is correct and .env has ENV='development'. Test failures under xdist loadscope are unrelated to this code.

context_for_next_testing_agent: The iter5 fix uses `useEffect(() => { if (!token) router.replace('/welcome'); }, [token, router])` on /lock, /set-pin, /settings. This fires during AuthProvider initial loading (before AsyncStorage rehydration completes), redirecting valid-session users to /welcome on any full page load / reload / goto to these routes. Fix must add `loading` from useAuth() to the predicate and deps. AuthProvider already exposes `loading` (see src/auth.tsx:8,27,107). To reproduce: register via UI → onboarding-skip → edit-back → /dashboard → page.goto('/settings') → observe redirect to /welcome despite localStorage/AsyncStorage having a valid token. Backend regression is fine (89/89 under loadfile). Frontend testIDs to reuse: register-email-input, register-password-input, register-confirm-input, register-submit-button, onboarding-skip, edit-back, dashboard-settings (WARN: Expo Web HMR duplicates this in DOM — prefer page.goto('/settings')), settings-change-pin, settings-lock-now, settings-signout, pin-key-{0..9}, pin-key-back, lock-signout, welcome-register-button, welcome-login-link, login-email-input, login-password-input, login-submit-button.
rca_of_issue: The iter5 fix intended to make signOut() on /lock deterministically redirect to /welcome by observing token in a useEffect. It works for the signOut case because signOut sets token=null AFTER loading has completed (loading=false), so the effect firing with !token correctly navigates. BUT the same useEffect also fires on FIRST mount, when the AuthProvider is still in its initial useEffect (auth.tsx:37-53): loading=true and token is null because tokenStorage.get() hasn't resolved yet. The screen therefore redirects to /welcome even though a valid token is present in storage. Reproduction: (1) Register (UI) → onboarding-skip → edit-back → /dashboard [state OK, no reload]. (2) page.goto('/settings') → new full load, AuthProvider re-mounts, useEffect on settings.tsx fires with token=null → replace('/welcome'). Observed URL after goto: /welcome. Expected: /settings. Same repro works with page.reload() on /lock and page.goto('/set-pin'). Mitigation: gate the redirect on !loading, i.e. `if (!loading && !token) router.replace('/welcome')` and add `loading` to deps.
